evidence.excerpt: The budget speech says the government had decided to introduce a universal pension system from the next fiscal year, framing it as a sustainable, organized social-security reform and noting that the draft law had already been prepared.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with an explicit reform announcement and implementation timeline.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and aimed at the next fiscal year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is a cabinet-level institutional reform under Hasina's government, with clear executive ownership even if the speech was delivered by the finance minister.
contrary_evidence: It is still an announced reform in 2022, not proof of completed rollout.
Old-age protection goals may face implementation and coverage limits after announcement.

evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The budget speech says the government had brought all government transactions under a Treasury Single Account and planned to move 100 percent of social safety-net allowances under the G2P system by FY2022-23, with a Uniform Social Register already developed in iBAS++.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech with specific administrative reforms and rollout status.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and described as already underway or scheduled for FY2022-23.

contrary_evidence: Administrative integration does not by itself show leakage reduction or better beneficiary targeting.

evidence.claim: Hasina said the government was looking for ways to bring essential prices within people's purchasing power, would sell rice to 5 million families at Tk 15 per kg, and would issue special family cards to 10 million people.
evidence.title: Govt trying to bring down prices of essentials: PM
evidence.excerpt: Hasina said the government was looking for ways to bring essential prices within people's purchasing power, would sell rice to 5 million families at Tk 15 per kg, and would issue special family cards to 10 million people.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and quoted remarks in the article
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a direct PM statement with concrete mitigation measures, though still secondary coverage.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within August 2022, during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High: this is a direct public response by Hasina at an ECNEC meeting, showing crisis-response ownership.
contrary_evidence: The response was reactive to a record price shock and did not by itself solve inflation or supply-side pressures.
The article shows intent and mitigation, not independently verified household-level impact.

evidence.claim: In a BBC interview, Hasina said people should judge for themselves how much truth there is in allegations of enforced disappearances and said free and fair elections were only possible under an Awami League government.

evidence.excerpt: In a BBC interview, Hasina said people should judge for themselves how much truth there is in allegations of enforced disappearances and said free and fair elections were only possible under an Awami League government.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous direct-quote reporting from a major Bangladeshi paper; secondary source but with specific on-record quotations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for the quoted remarks because they are first-person statements by Hasina; low for any inference of admission because the remarks are defensive, not corrective.
contrary_evidence: The quote is not an admission, correction, or disclosure of wrongdoing; it is a denial or deflection.
No self-correction is stated in the passage.
